title: The Self-Improving OSS Agent Stack — Marc Klingen, Langfuse
talk_summary: Langfuse's Marc Klingen describes a loop hierarchy where humans set direction (datasets, eval criteria) while AI automates the tedious lower loops: mining production traces for failure patterns, proposing new evals/datasets, and hill-climbing agent implementations against them. He demos a changelog-writer agent that uses human PR review feedback (approvals/change requests) as signal to auto-improve its own prompts and evals.

takeaways.what_they_do: Human review actions on agent output (PR approvals, change requests, edit ratio) are captured as production signal and fed back to propose new eval criteria and dataset cases for the agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: both of these kinds of like either like approvals or uh requests for changes can get feed into like the AI obserability and eval to to serve as a basis for auto improvement

takeaways.technique: Edit-ratio and jargon metrics as evaluators
takeaways.what_they_do: They instrumented the agent's output with concrete metrics (edit ratio of human change requests, jargon leakage, clarity) and used them as eval dimensions to compare v1 baseline vs v2 candidate before merging.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the edit ratio of us humans making ch like submitting change requests is still high and that we leak internal jargon to our customers

takeaways.technique: Baseline-vs-candidate backtest before adopting agent changes
takeaways.what_they_do: When the agent proposes an implementation change, they run old (v1 baseline) and new (v2 candidate) against the same updated dataset and only adopt on positive delta across all eval dimensions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can back test it basically on the updated data set to see whether the new implementation would do better than the old implementation

takeaways.technique: Scheduled batch loop over accumulated signal
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of continuous self-modification, they run the improvement agent as a cron job over a batch of interesting production data (daily/weekly), keeping humans at the goal-setting boundary.
takeaways.evidence_quote: run agents like on a loop uh usually like a crown job like every day every week whenever you have like a batch of basically interesting user data

takeaways.technique: Human owns eval boundary, AI owns proposals
takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly keep humans in the loop for dataset alignment and eval criteria because agents otherwise overfit to irrelevant production quirks; AI is used mainly to propose fixes within that boundary.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you maintain the boundary of what you optimize against. And you use AI mostly for like proposing improvements

takeaways.technique: Own the trace data layer, expect read-heavy workloads
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue for retaining full unsampled traces long-term in a self-owned store because agent loops are now read-intensive, chewing through historical traces as context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Now it's way more read intensive because agents can like like chew through so much more data
